name: hydrogen, atom by atom
plain: Computed as you watch by this repository's engine (holon-render's Sim, through holon-draw-atoms): one H2 molecule, started stretched 15% and turning with kT at 300 K, in the engine's 24-bohr walled box (the frame), followed by its first atom. The pair curve is the engine's own: H2 in the STO-3G basis, full CI (holon-chem), computed ahead of time on the 492 knots the atoms page solves on load and built in (holon-draw-atoms/data/h2_sto3g.json; R_e 1.3887 bohr, D_e 0.2041 Eh), because the solve takes over a second. Exact in that model, not a prediction of experiment. No three-body table is loaded; two atoms need none. Atoms are drawn as the engine draws them, as balls of half that bond length.

carrier.state: one H2 molecule: two nuclei on the engine's full-CI curve

basis.note: 'Every rung is centred on ONE point going in': each finer rung is drawn about the point the coarser one shows at its centre. The same file names this rung 'the exception it has to be': the live simulation is of H2, not of water, so the atom this rung centres on is a hydrogen atom of H2 and not the water molecule's that the chain follows.

views.reads: the rung's marks at the zoom's metres per pixel

budget.quantity: what drawing a tile coarse may move against drawing it fine: the draw allocator's tolerance (Acuity, eps_px). It is not a bound on the picture's faithfulness to the holon.
